task_metadata.research_topic: global pooling and feature aggregation design for CNN-based image classification
task_metadata.research_question: Design a novel global pooling or feature aggregation strategy for image classification that improves test accuracy across different CNN architectures and datasets.
notes: The GeM baseline maps directly to the generalized-mean pooling paper used in the baseline edit stub.

The avg_max baseline is linked approximately to CBAM because CBAM explicitly combines global average and max pooled descriptors, while the repo baseline uses the same statistics without learned attention weights.
The global_max baseline is left as no_explicit_paper because the repo baseline names a standard operator rather than a uniquely attributable standalone method paper.
CIFAR-based tests are linked to their architecture papers; a dedicated auditable BibTeX source for the original CIFAR technical report was not recovered through MCP during this run.

tests.label: resnet56-cifar100
tests.notes: ResNet-56 evaluation linked to the canonical ResNet paper.

tests.label: vgg16bn-cifar100
tests.notes: VGG-16-BN evaluation linked to the VGG architecture paper.

tests.label: mobilenetv2-fmnist
tests.notes: Hidden evaluation links MobileNetV2 and Fashion-MNIST.

baselines.name: global_max
baselines.notes: The baseline is a standard adaptive global max pooling operator, but the stub does not point to a uniquely attributable standalone method paper.

baselines.name: gem
baselines.notes: Direct match to the GeM pooling method named in the baseline edit.

baselines.name: avg_max
baselines.notes: Approximate match to CBAM, which explicitly combines global average and max pooled statistics before channel reweighting.

papers.title: Network In Network
papers.relevance: Canonical introduction of global average pooling in CNN classifiers, which is the default family of methods this task asks agents to improve on.
